HazardPulse model (hurricane_ri_v10-8a5ba5896731) — our own rapid-intensification forecast, shown for comparison. The published number is NOAA’s until the pre-registered test below is passed.

  • What it is: Our own model: one exceedance curve P(a rise of k kt in 24 h), k = 15–45, from the early intensity guidance (NOAA’s statistical models, the hurricane and global models, NHC’s consensus aids), NOAA’s RI probabilities at six thresholds and the official forecast; NOAA’s DTOPS wherever that guidance is missing
  • Each season 2022–2025: predicted from earlier seasons only: log loss 0.144 vs DTOPS 0.165 (paired by storm [−0.031, −0.010]); over DTOPS’s four 24-h thresholds, Brier 0.155 vs 0.172 [−0.028, −0.006]
  • Against every RI probability NOAA publishes: 2022–2025, as served, each season predicted from earlier ones; 30-kt log loss SHIPS-RII 0.200 (ours 0.144) · RI logistic 0.197 (ours 0.144) · RI Bayesian 0.232 (ours 0.144) · RI consensus 0.183 (ours 0.144) · DTOPS 0.166 (ours 0.148): ours is lower than every one, each paired by storm with its 95% interval below zero
  • Against intensity forecasts as yes/no RI calls: at each call’s own false-alarm rate (a forecast 24-h rise of 30 kt or more), ours catches more RI events than SHIPS (DSHP) (+19 points [+6, +31]); and is within noise of NHC official forecast · HCCA · IVCN · LGEM · NNIC · GEFS mean · hurricane-model mean · most aggressive hurricane model · global-model mean (gaps −3 to +9 points)
  • 2026 so far: log loss 0.129 vs DTOPS 0.150, AUC 0.925 (a second look at a season that informed its design, so not a proof)
  • Challenger in shadow (v10.2): hurricane_ri_v10_2-3e9c1b766454: the same inputs, never lowering the odds when the guidance or NOAA’s probability rises. 2022–2025 against v10.1: log loss 0.1436 vs 0.1443 [−0.0022, +0.0008], four-threshold Brier 0.1544 vs 0.1554; a gain whose interval still includes zero; 2026 (a later look at a season that informed the design, not a proof): 0.1262 vs 0.1291. Scored live with its own prospective test at 99.375%; it replaces the shown model only by the rule written before it scored a cycle
  • Challenger in shadow (v10.3): hurricane_ri_v10_3-f941a72e2682: v10.2 plus the storm’s cloud-top structure from satellite infrared (NOAA GMGSI, two hours after the cycle and six hours earlier). 2022–2025 against v10.2: log loss 0.1418 vs 0.1436 [−0.0054, +0.0015], four-threshold Brier 0.1527 vs 0.1544; a gain whose interval still includes zero; 2026 (a later look at a season that informed the design, not a proof): 0.1178 vs 0.1262 [−0.0152, −0.0018]. Scored live with its own prospective test at 99.6875%; it replaces the shown model only by the rule written before it scored a cycle
  • Status: in prospective verification: shown beside NOAA’s number, not instead of it, until the pre-registered prospective test on cycles from 2026-10-04 meets its rule (verdicts 2026-12-01 and 2027-12-01); cycles scored so far: 0

Where the RI number comes from: Atlantic, East and Central Pacific: NOAA's rapid-intensification guidance read from NHC's SHIPS text for the same cycle -- DTOPS as issued, and SHIPS-RII where DTOPS is missing -- chosen by a pre-registered comparison on 2020-2024 and scored once on 2025 (docs/HURRICANE_RI_PROGRAM.md). West Pacific, Indian Ocean, Southern Hemisphere (no public RI guidance) and any NHC cycle without a usable SHIPS text: HazardPulse v8.2.

Source feed: /data/live-storms.json. Always follow official advisories from the National Hurricane Center and local authorities.
